decisions.reason: As a bread loaf close to the core assortment, it fits existing skills and resources well, and with no clear negative performance signal in a growing industry management would likely retain it unless sales clearly fell below aspiration.

The sweet pastry is also close to the established offer, but pastries are easier to rotate within a medium-sized assortment, so it faces somewhat more pruning risk despite the absence of evidence of clear underperformance.

This farmhouse bread uses the firm's traditional baking capabilities and likely benefits from stable everyday demand, so under behavioral decision making it would usually be kept unless it persistently underperformed relative to comparable breads.

The poppy seed Christmas stollen is an award-winning seasonal specialty that appears to perform above aspiration and strongly matches the firm's heritage-based positioning, making withdrawal unlikely.
The premium Christmas stollen also carries a gold-award signal and fits the firm's festive, high-quality reputation, so management would have little reason to reallocate resources away from it.
